Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications from Finova legal: 

1) On controller vs processor: Finova treats customer account and billing data as controller-owned. For telemetry/usage metrics, can you confirm whether Redwood acts as processor or if any combined controller decisions happen (e.g., joint analytics used for product improvements)?

2) SCC modules: our counsel usually prefers Module Two (standard processor-to-controller) for SaaS vendors, but they want to see a short rationale why Redwood would recommend Module X vs Module Y.

3) SOC 2 evidence: we can accept a summary report initially; legal will request the full report under an NDA.

4) Preferred route for contracts: DocuSign is fine. Please send the draft DPA and indicate which SCC module you recommend and why.

Finova legal contact for routing: Legal Intake <legal@finovasys.com> — looping them in on follow-up.

Sarah — thanks for the quick reply and the routing info. I’m Redwood’s privacy counsel; I’ve attached a proposed DPA (RW_DPA_Proposed_v1.pdf) and a short SCC module comparison (SCC_Module_Comparison.xlsx) that addresses the points below. Key items: 

Controller / Processor position
- Redwood’s baseline position: we act as a processor for data ingested on behalf of our customers (Finova) when we process customer content to provide inference services. We do not assert a controller role for customer content.
- Telemetry & product analytics: telemetry is collected under our standard terms to run, secure, and improve the service. Where telemetry contains deidentified metrics tied to product improvement, we treat that as operational processing; we can offer options to limit analytics as contract terms (e.g., opt-out clauses, narrower retention).

SCC module recommendation
- Recommended starting point: Module Two (Processor to Controller safeguards) since your counsel indicated SaaS relationship and Finova is the data controller for customer content.
- Rationale: Module Two maps to our standard responsibilities (technical controls, subprocessors, onward transfer rules). We include an option in the DPA for Module Three fallback if Finova’s downstream flows require different export controls.

SOC 2 and HIPAA
- SOC 2 Type II: we completed our 2025 Type II and can provide a summary report immediately and full report under NDA.
- HIPAA: Redwood offers a BAA for customers handling PHI. For production PHI workloads we advise Private deployment; the DPA includes fields to document whether BAA terms apply.

Next steps we propose
- Please review the attached DPA and the SCC comparison. If Module Two is acceptable, we’ll insert that module into the DPA and prepare a DocuSign envelope.
- Proposed 30-min review with Finova legal on Thu Nov 5 at 11:00 PST — Logan will send a calendar invite. 

Attachments: RW_DPA_Proposed_v1.pdf (track-changes friendly), SCC_Module_Comparison.xlsx (one-pager).

If you want any alternate language around telemetry opt-out or data retention caps, flag them and we’ll propose contract language.

— Marissa Cole
